open_decisions.title: Restricted collision telemetry for a SHA-256 uniqueness collision is not emitted
open_decisions.note: SEARCH_CRAWL_RETRIEVAL.md § Frontier And Deterministic Selection sets four obligations on a hash collision: retain both SHA-256 and full preimage, allocate a collision ordinal, NEVER merge candidates, and 'emit restricted collision telemetry and follow the Volume I integrity result' (also AC-SM-006). S-07-004 implements the first three; the fourth is NOT built — the tranche creates no telemetry surface and the frontier is a technical execution record with no ledger writer of its own. Practical risk is nil (a SHA-256 collision cannot occur), so this is a record-honesty item, not a defect: the migration comment was corrected from claiming exact conformance. The same obligation applies to every other deduplication_keys consumer, so it belongs with a platform telemetry surface rather than S-07.

open_decisions.title: The same-Organization CROSS-PROJECT defect class has now appeared in three consecutive tranches
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-079 (S-07-005 security lens); prior instances ADR-076 CB5, ADR-078 CB5
open_decisions.note: POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md :128 requires every Project-owned child-to-parent reference to carry all three of (organization_id, project_id, id), 'rather than a separate Project lookup or application assertion'. S-07-003 shipped a two-column FK on evaluation_orchestration_contexts; S-07-004 shipped one on crawl_frontier_entries.scope_policy_id; S-07-005 shipped the same defect in the READ PATH, where no FK can enforce it (FetchAuthorization read the Source and its scope policy by (organization, source) alone, so a Crawl in Project A could be authorized under Project B's scope). Each was found by review and fixed, but the recurrence rate is the finding: the rule is easy to violate silently and nothing mechanically detects it. RECOMMENDED: an architecture fitness spec that fails when any FK to a Project-owned parent has arity < 3, and a companion check or convention for Project-scoped reads. Not an S-07 dependency; no S-07 contract obligation is unmet.

open_decisions.title: Sitemap discovery has no scheduler re-entry after sustained host-gate contention
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-081 (ADR-026 concurrency lens, non-blocking with a named trigger)
open_decisions.note: A host under sustained contention can exhaust MAX_DEFERRALS_PER_CANDIDATE and terminalize `sitemap_unavailable` with zero network attempts — write-once, coverage partial. Mitigated (the gate now reports the REAL remaining wait, so pacing no longer expires on a legitimate Crawl-delay) but not closed. S-07-008 owns run scheduling and MUST provide the re-entry; if it does not, this becomes a coverage defect and reopens S-07-006. MITIGATED, NOT DELIVERED, by S-07-008 (b1dcea9), and NOT closed. The ADR-026 architecture and concurrency lenses were right that a hand-back method is not scheduler re-entry: nothing in production calls `DiscoverSitemaps#call` at all, so 'the next pass claims it exactly as the first did' presupposes a pass that does not exist. What S-07-008 genuinely removed is the write-once FALSE outcome: sustained contention no longer terminalizes. :450 conditions `sitemap_unavailable` on 'no candidate succeeds AFTER retries/validation'; a candidate the rate limiter never released has had neither, so nothing is recorded - the claim is handed back (`release_sitemaps`, token-bound), the gate returns to `pending`, and the next pass claims it exactly as the first did. NO new scheduled-action kind: the catalogue is closed and a `pending` gate IS the re-entry. Bounded by the run's wall clock, past which discovery terminalizes `unavailable` once, honestly. NOT closed until the five ADR-026 lenses report (ADR-080). The DRIVER is now owned by BUILD_PLAN S-07-012 (Crawl Execution - the run driver), which must honour the `retry_after` instant the release reports and must also re-enter `Admission`'s `run_byte_budget_contended` outcome. FU-9 closes when S-07-012 lands, not before. A SECOND defect found by the same review and repaired here: the run-wide sitemap-document budget was charged BEFORE the gate was consulted and had no release path, so every deferred pass shrank the budget and the re-entry converged on the very `sitemap_unavailable` outcome FU-9 exists to prevent; the charge now happens once per distinct URL at the moment an attempt genuinely begins.

open_decisions.title: Ordered budget admission (:456's coordinator) is owed by S-07-008
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-082 (ADR-026 contract lens, confirmed-blocking, scoped to S-07-008)
open_decisions.note: :456 — 'one coordinator commits discoveries and budget effects in increasing dequeue key. A completion with a later key waits in fetched_pending_commit.' S-07-007 enforces the SUM (verified under eight simultaneous workers) and materializes dequeue_key on every fetch_attempts row so the order can be applied without re-deriving it. S-07-008 owns the coordinator. Until it exists, byte admission at the run boundary is nondeterministic, which :456 forbids ('Selection under every finite bound is deterministic'). DELIVERED S-07-008 (508edde): `Wf005::Admission` claims the frontier entry AND its byte reservation in ONE transaction under the frontier's own advisory lock, so admission order equals dequeue order by construction - no coordinator, no pending queue. The `fetched_pending_commit` limb of :456 concerns committing a fetched document's DISCOVERIES in dequeue order; link extraction is S-07-010's and that limb belongs with it. The lock is proved load-bearing by BLOCKING, not by racing. NOT closed until the five ADR-026 lenses report (ADR-080).

open_decisions.title: A terminal Crawl may carry NULL coverage_status and NULL completion_reason
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 schema lens at S-07-008 (third pass, MISDIAGNOSED) corrected by the fourth pass, which evaluated both forms against the live cluster.
open_decisions.note: CORRECTED TWICE. Pass three recorded this as a three-valued-logic hole in `crawls_coverage_status_check` and prescribed the `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` form. THAT PRESCRIPTION IS A PROVEN NO-OP: evaluated live, `NULL = ANY(ARRAY['full','partial'])` yields UNKNOWN (admitted) and the NULL-safe rewrite yields TRUE (also admitted). `schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md` declares the column nullable, which is what a non-terminal Crawl needs. THE ACTUAL DEFECT is in `crawls_terminal_shape` and it is ordinary two-valued logic: its terminal limb requires only `terminal_at IS NOT NULL`, so `state='completed'` with `coverage_status` and `completion_reason` both NULL satisfies every constraint on the table. THE REPAIR, corrected by the pass-four schema lens, is a terminal-completeness conjunct SCOPED BY STATE: every terminal state requires `completion_reason IS NOT NULL`, and `state='completed'` additionally requires `coverage_status IS NOT NULL`. The earlier 'a terminal Crawl must carry BOTH columns' form is wrong and would break `IdentityAccess::Infrastructure::CrawlStartStore#fail`, which sets `state='failed'` with a completion reason and no coverage. Reconcile the catalogue's nullable declaration with the same rule. BLOCKING FOR S-07-009, which writes exactly those two columns. The three genuine three-valued-logic holes found by the same sweep are separate and non-blocking: `identity_receipt_nonces.bootstrap_digest_only_for_bootstrap_purposes`, `invitations.invitation_active_expiry_is_seven_days`, `projects.projects_local_profile_shape`.

open_decisions.title: Non-blocking backlog carried out of S-07-008's third review pass
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 lenses at S-07-008, third pass. Recorded rather than repaired, to avoid widening an unaccepted tranche.
open_decisions.note: (a) `crawl_limit_decisions.decided_by_service_identity_id` carries NO FK to `service_identities`, unlike every other Service-Identity reference in the schema, so `Platform::ServiceIdentity`'s 'existence is guaranteed by the ledger foreign keys' does not hold for it and the migration's 'a limit decision has an author' is unenforced. (b) `specification/automation/BUILD_PLAN.yml` DOES NOT PARSE AS YAML (Psych: could not find expected ':' at line 506) - PRE-EXISTING at both endpoints of the S-07-008 range, but it weakens the guarantee that the controller reads `depends_on`, which S-07-009's new comment rests on. (c) `DECISIONS.md` ADR-081 still reads 'that re-entry is S-07-008's' with no supersession note; the reassignment to S-07-012 must be carried into whatever ADR accepts S-07-008. (d) `crawl_sitemap_document_charges` lacks `UNIQUE (organization_id, project_id, id)`, which every sibling crawl table carries per POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA :128 - no live defect (nothing FKs to it) but a future child could not form the three-column link. (e) WITHDRAWN - the index `crawl_sitemap_document_charges_crawl` is NOT dead and must not be dropped. It was recorded as dead from a scan count taken BEFORE the same commit made it load-bearing: `charged_count` and the projection recompute both resolve through its `(organization_id, crawl_id)` prefix, and the ledger's ceiling enforcement now depends on it. Retained here as a correction rather than deleted, because a backlog item that directs the removal of a load-bearing index is exactly the false premise this review exists to catch. (f) `EffectiveLimits.resolve`'s rescue is method-wide, so ONE unparseable policy discards EVERY valid narrowing policy; behaviour is unchanged from the copies it replaced but this is now the canonical statement. (g) once the sitemap budget is spent, remaining candidates still claim and release a real host-gate slot and re-run FetchAuthorization before discovering they cannot pay.

open_decisions.title: Two live tables are absent from the canonical schema catalogue (pre-existing)
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 schema lens at S-07-008, fourth pass; now enforced by spec/architecture/repository_truth_spec.rb
open_decisions.note: `role_expiry_block_decisions` (WF-013, T-IMM, forced RLS) has no row in schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md. `evidence` is catalogued under the name `evidences`, which no table carries - so the real table appears under no name and the catalogue names one that does not exist. BOTH PRE-EXISTING at 09277e7, neither introduced by S-07-008, and both are explicitly allowlisted in the repository-truth check rather than silently absorbed: the check now fails on any NEW omission. Resolving `evidence`/`evidences` requires deciding which name is ratified - the migration's or the catalogue's - which is an owner call, not an implementer's.

reconciliation_note: NOTE ON THE COMMIT FIELDS: they name the commit they DESCRIBE, which is necessarily the one before the commit that records them - writing a SHA into a file changes that file's own commit SHA. Amending to close the loop orphans the recorded object, which the repository-truth spec now catches as unreachable. 2026-07-29 (S-07-008: NOT ACCEPTED, blocked). Four independent ADR-026 five-lens passes have run. The implementation converged; the REPOSITORY RECORD did not - each pass found false claims in artefacts the previous pass had rewritten, and the fourth found a status token invented for this file that the controller's own validator rejects. Owner decision: reduce the claim surface rather than re-review a growing account of it. In flight: three runtime repairs (the queue/depth population must be ONE definition shared by count, eviction eligibility and observation; the wall-clock soft observation must be independent of hard exhaustion; the ledger must reproduce its own identity from its stored bytes), four proof gaps, a mechanically bounded acceptance record, and automated repository-truth checks. FU-11 is MISDIAGNOSED and being corrected: the admission is `crawls_terminal_shape` lacking a terminal-completeness conjunct, not a three-valued-logic hole, and its prescribed `IS NULL OR` repair is a proven no-op. FU-12(e) is being corrected: the index it calls dead is load-bearing for the ledger bound. Verified at this commit: rspec 1882/0; brakeman, packwerk, zeitwerk clean; verify_runtime 15 checks; no structure drift.
next_action: S-07-008 (Crawl Execution - limits, soft/hard events, wall clock) is IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE and has been through FIVE independent ADR-026 review passes: four full five-lens passes and a fifth scoped to mutation testing of the reduced acceptance surface. It is NOT ACCEPTED and no ADR is allocated. The remaining work is the owner's acceptance decision, not further review. FU-10 (:456 ordered admission) is delivered here. FU-9 is MITIGATED, not delivered: this tranche removed the write-once false `sitemap_unavailable` and the budget leak behind it, but scheduler re-entry needs a DRIVER, which is BUILD_PLAN S-07-012 and is encoded in S-07-009's depends_on. The once-per-run event mechanism is `crawl_limit_decisions` UNIQUE (crawl_id, limit_dimension, threshold_kind); the counter-bit claim on `crawl_budget_counters` was superseded and DELETED, and nothing reads `soft_limit_events`/`hard_limit_events`. FU-11 gates S-07-009 and its diagnosis has been corrected twice - the fault is `crawls_terminal_shape`, not `crawls_coverage_status_check`, and the repair is a terminal-completeness conjunct scoped by state. Repository claims that were previously carried by prose are now asserted by spec/architecture/repository_truth_spec.rb.

excluded_contamination.owner_ruling: 2026-07-29. Published history is NOT rewritten to make the tranche cosmetically clean. The unrelated files are explicitly EXCLUDED from the S-07-008 acceptance diff and the contamination is recorded here. History surgery would only be justified if the branch were private, nothing were based on it, governance permitted rewriting, and separation materially improved release/audit/cherry-pick integrity - which is not established.
excluded_contamination.reason: S-07-008 (1/n) and (2/n) were committed with `git add -A`, sweeping in parallel branding/investor/operations work. Commits 3/n onward stage engineering paths explicitly.
excluded_contamination.note: 827c39a is therefore NOT an atomic implementation unit. Review S-07-008 by PATH over the commit range, never by treating that commit as the tranche's first slice.

acceptance_evidence.verified: The path-scoped diff plus the excluded set together account for every file changed in the range; nothing falls outside both.
acceptance_evidence.note_on_range: Stated as a path-scoped range against the branch head rather than a fixed SHA: the record of the exclusion necessarily lives in a commit AFTER any SHA it could name, so a fixed endpoint would exclude its own declaration. The invariant that matters is the one verified below, and it is re-checkable at any head.
acceptance_evidence.note_on_paths: `schemas/` was missing from the first declaration, which made a table existing in the database but not in the canonical catalogue structurally invisible to the declared review procedure. Found by the third-pass schema and architecture lenses.
